title: Bounded finite-projective model of a locally strictly perfect stalk
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], E an object of D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category], x a point, and G a cochain complex with Q(G) isomorphic to E. Suppose there is a neighbourhood V of x on which E is represented by a strictly perfect complex [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Then there exist a complex L of modules over R = O_X,x [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] and integers a,b such that L is zero outside [a,b], every L^j is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and Q(L) is isomorphic to Q(G_x) in D(R). The morphism universes of D(R) and D(O_X) may differ. No assertion about residue cohomology is made.

source.place: Tags 00A0(3), 01AG, 08C4 and 08CM: open restriction, exact stalks and strictly perfect complexes

proof.text: Destructure hlocal to choose V, its point y=(x,hx), P, its strict-perfect bounds a,b and eP. Set S=openModuleStalkFunctor X V y and construct L termwise as S(P). Preservation of zero morphisms gives preservation of zero objects, hence the bounds for L.

For the finite-generation helper, the unit-stalk isomorphism in ideal_module_product_stalk, the equivalence of the over site with the open subscheme and restrictionScalarsIsoOfEquiv identify S(unit) with the ambient stalk ring. PreservesCoproduct.iso takes S(free ULift(Fin m)) to the coproduct of m copies of S(unit). Reindex by Equiv.ulift.symm, identify the finite coproduct with its biproduct and use ModuleCat.biproductIsoPi. Module.Finite.equiv transfers finite generation of the finite product to S(free). This also works for m=0.

In each degree apply S to the two maps of the finite-free retraction supplied by IsStrictlyPerfect. Functor.map_comp and map_id verify the retraction equation. The finite free stalk is projective by openModuleStalk_free_projective, so Retract.projective and the ModuleCat comparison instance give Module.Projective of L.X j. The retraction equation explicitly gives surjectivity of S(pi); Module.Finite.of_surjective and the preceding helper give finite generation.

Use the exactness instances of S and Mathlib Functor.mapDerivedCategoryFactors to map eP and eG, obtaining Q(L) isomorphic to Q(S(R(G))), where R is open restriction. Apply nonempty_restriction_stalk_extension_iso to G. Use the chain isomorphism induced by Modules.overFunctorEquiv to identify over-site restriction with open-subscheme restriction. Restrict the resulting extension-stalk comparison back along the open immersion stalk-ring map. That map is an isomorphism, hence its scalar restriction is an equivalence and the extension/restriction adjunction unit is invertible. Its termwise chain isomorphism cancels the scalar extension. Compose these chain isomorphisms and apply Q.mapIso to obtain the stated derived isomorphism. The exact-functor API allows the two morphism universes to differ.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_localStrictPerfect_stalk_projective_model
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X) (x : X)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{v} (ModuleCat.{u} (X.presheaf.stalk x))]
    (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (eG : DerivedCategory.Q.obj G ≅ E)
    (hlocal : ∃ V : X.Opens, x ∈ V ∧
      ∃ P : CochainComplex
          (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V)) ℤ,
        IsStrictlyPerfect X V P ∧
        Nonempty ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
          (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) V).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ≅
          DerivedCategory.Q.obj P))
    : ∃ (L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (X.presheaf.stalk x)) ℤ)
      (a b : ℤ),
      (∀ j : ℤ, j < a ∨ b < j → IsZero (L.X j)) ∧
      (∀ j : ℤ, Module.Finite (X.presheaf.stalk x) (L.X j) ∧
        Module.Projective (X.presheaf.stalk x) (L.X j)) ∧
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj G))
